newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Bomb in southeast Nigerian oil city kills one.
newsitem.headline: Bomb in southeast Nigerian oil city kills one.

text.p: A bomb explosion in Nigeria's southeastern oil city of Port Harcourt killed a 12-year-old boy and wounded his two companions on Wednesday, police said on Thursday.

"We have confirmed that it was a bomb and experts are now checking what remains," a senior police officer said by telephone from Port Harcourt. He said he did not know who was responsible and that there were no suspects at this stage.

Military-ruled Nigeria has been hit by a spate of bomb blasts since last year, most of which have targeted soldiers. The last one, in May, killed two people at a mosque in the eastern city of Onitsha.
Local newspapers said the victims of the Port Harcourt bomb were street hawkers and that there was no military target nearby.
"An explosive device concealed in a tin wrapped in a polythene bag was detonated by one of the boys who picked it up as it was thrown from a moving vehicle," the independent Guardian newspaper said.
Twelve opposition activists including exiled Nobel prize laureate Wole Soyinka have been charged with treason in a Lagos magistrates court over the bombings.
The umbrella opposition group the National Democratic Coalition, which is accused by the police of involvement, has denied having anything to do with the attacks.
Port Harcourt is the principal base for oil companies operating in southeastern Nigeria. The West African country pumps more than two million barrels of crude oil every day.
